Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Mumbai man pays Livspace Rs 71.62 lakh for premium flat interiors, finds inferior materials and exposed live wires, wife suffers head injury after heavy kitchen shutter falls on her; consumer commissi
Article Text:
(AI image) Livspace India Pvt Ltd has been held responsible for unsafe renovation work in a Goregaon flat.





MUMBAI: The Maharashtra State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held interior design firm Livspace India Pvt Ltd guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practices over a Goregaon flat renovation that left exposed live wires and saw a heavy kitchen shutter fall on a woman's head.The commission expressed grave concern over the company's alleged negligence and hazardous workmanship, observing that it had promised premium materials and branded products, including its “Regalia” modular kitchen range, but systematically substituted them with inferior alternatives.“This bait-and-switch tactic constitutes an unfair trade practice, as it misleads consumers regarding the standard, quality, and grade of services and goods promised,” the commission said.It directed Livspace to pay complainant Deepak Ruiya nearly Rs 87.16 lakh, comprising a refund of Rs 71.62 lakh and Rs 15.54 lakh in interest and compensation. The commission also found that the company had failed to complete the renovation within the agreed timeline, used inferior materials and left the premises in an unsafe condition.“The record evidences severe safety breaches, including uninsulated live electrical wires left exposed behind bed panels, posing a life-threatening hazard to the complainant’s children and elderly family members.Furthermore, the installation was so shoddy that a heavy kitchen shutter collapsed directly onto the complainant’s wife's head,” it said.The commission also flagged the company's administrative chaos and lack of professional oversight. It noted that senior designers and project personnel exited without notice, while Livspace changed project managers and designers without Ruiya's consent, leaving the project without proper supervision for months.“This erratic management directly contributed to substandard execution and severe delay,” the commission observed.Ruiya filed the complaint in 2025 against Livspace India Pvt Ltd, formerly known as Home Interior Designs E-Commerce Pvt Ltd. He had hired the company to design and renovate his flat at Kalpataru Radiance in Goregaon West for Rs 71.62 lakh.Livspace had assured him that the work would be completed within 90 to 120 days. The original handover deadline was July 1, 2024, which was later extended to September 1, 2024.According to Ruiya, despite substantial payments, the project remained incomplete, with designers and managers being changed without notice. He also alleged that the company used lower-grade materials instead of those promised, including HDHMR instead of the specified grade of plywood and “Infiniti” shutters instead of the “Regalia” range.The complaint also highlighted serious safety lapses. Ruiya alleged that live electrical wires were left uninsulated behind bed panels and that, on January 2, 2025, a heavy kitchen shutter fell on his wife’s head due to faulty installation.After issuing a legal notice on December 5, 2024, he approached the commission seeking a refund, compensation and litigation costs.Livspace failed to appear before the commission despite being served notice and a newspaper publication. The matter consequently proceeded ex parte in July 2025.The commission noted that Ruiya's affidavit, payment records, emails, photographs and survey material remained unrebutted. It held that the company's failure to meet even the extended deadline and its substitution of promised materials with inferior alternatives amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.Apart from refunding the amount paid with interest, Livspace was directed to pay compensation for mental agony, harassment and the safety risks caused, along with litigation costs.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has held interior design firm Livspace India Pvt Ltd guilty of deficiency in service and unfair trade practices. The commission expressed grave concern over the company's alleged negligence and hazardous workmanship. It directed Livspace to pay complainant Deepak Ruiya nearly Rs 87.16 lakh.

Article Title: India, Oman begin naval exercise as Arabian Sea security takes centre stage
Article Text:
INS Surat at the Port of Muscat in Oman for a bilateral exercise. (Image credit: Indian Navy)

Why these waters matter

Working with partners in the region

A large share of India's crude oil imports and exports passes through the Arabian Sea and the western Indian Ocean. Any disruption in these waters can quickly affect freight rates, insurance costs and supply chains.Against this backdrop, Indian Naval Ship (INS) Surat arrived in Muscat, Oman, on November 8 to participate in the 15th edition of the bilateral maritime exercise Naseem Al Bahr, followed by a Coordinated Patrol (CORPAT) with the Royal Navy of Oman.The exercise includes harbour and sea phases, with cross-deck visits, operational interactions and sporting events. The aim is to allow personnel from both navies to exchange operational experience and best practices, improve interoperability and strengthen mutual understanding.The port call is in line with the government's MAHASAGAR vision, short for Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions. It also builds on the 13th meeting of the India-Oman Joint Military Cooperation Committee, held on November 24, 2025.Press Information Bureau+1The western maritime approaches connect India's ports with the Gulf, the Red Sea, Europe and the east coast of Africa. The Gulf of Aden and the waters off Somalia are particularly important because they provide access to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal, a major shipping route between Asia and Europe.Any disruption caused by conflict, piracy or attacks on merchant vessels can affect India's energy security and export industries.The Indian Navy has maintained an anti-piracy deployment in the Gulf of Aden since 2008. In July 2026, INS Trikand responded to an attempted pirate attack on the merchant vessel MV Golden Arsenal, approximately 300 nautical miles (550 km) east-northeast of Djibouti. The warship deployed a boarding team, supported by a P-8I maritime patrol aircraft, to secure the vessel and assess the situation.In 2026, the Navy also launched Operation Urja Suraksha to protect merchant shipping and India's energy interests amid the worsening security situation in West Asia.Its role extends beyond anti-piracy patrols. INS Tarkash, deployed in the western Indian Ocean from January 2025, supported Combined Task Force 150 of the 47-nation Combined Maritime Forces (CMF). On March 31, 2025, the warship intercepted a vessel carrying more than 2,500 kg of narcotics.On October 14, 2026, the Indian Navy relinquished command of Combined Task Force 154, the CMF's maritime training task force, at a ceremony in Bahrain. During its eight-month command, the Navy oversaw multinational training and capacity-building initiatives involving personnel from 39 countries.INS Trikand visited Maputo, Mozambique, in March 2026, where it conducted joint training with the Mozambique Navy. On departure, the warship also undertook joint surveillance of Mozambique's exclusive economic zone, with Mozambican naval personnel on board.INS Sunayna's deployments under the IOS SAGAR initiative in 2025 and 2026 further demonstrated India's efforts to strengthen regional maritime cooperation. The 2025 mission included 44 naval personnel from nine partner countries, while the 2026 deployment brought together 38 personnel from 16 partner nations for multinational training and operational engagements across the Indian Ocean region.The Navy's operational reach was on display again on November 2, when INS Kolkata, supported by Indian Air Force assets, helped rescue all 20 crew members of the Iranian fishing vessel Azini, which had been hijacked by armed pirates off Somalia.The operation, conducted over 48 hours more than 3,000 km from Mumbai, involved maritime surveillance, marine commandos and an IAF C-17 aircraft that airdropped additional personnel. The crew was rescued without casualties.
Article Summary: A large share of India's crude oil imports and exports passes through the Arabian Sea and the western Indian Ocean. Any disruption in these waters can quickly affect freight rates, insurance costs and supply chains. The Indian Navy has maintained an anti-piracy deployment in the Gulf of Aden since 2008.

Article Title: As board weighs CEO Jensen Huang's 'exit', Nvidia shares fall 8% after report of second affair
Article Text:
Nvidia stocks had gained in actual stock market trading before the reports on board considering CEO's ouster

Nvidia shares fell 8 per cent in after-hours trading on Wednesday after reports that the company's board was preparing to discuss the future of CEO Jensen Huang amid allegations of two extramarital relationships, including one involving a businesswoman suspected by US intelligence officials of having links to Chinese intelligence services.After-hours trading takes place after the regular market session closes and is not necessarily representative of how a stock will perform when the market reopens.Nvidia's stock has come under significant pressure amid the controversy, with the company losing around $430 billion in market value over Monday and Tuesday as its shares fell a combined 9.5%. However, Nvidia shares had recovered 2.9% during Wednesday's regular trading session before plunging more than 8% after the closing bell.This comes as the Wall Street Journal, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that Nvidia's board was preparing to meet as early as Thursday to discuss Huang's future. CBS News reporter also said in a post on X that the board was preparing to discuss the CEO's position, with the Trump administration aware of plans to remove him. Various reports have also claimed that the board is reportedly looking for a temporary chief to take over from Huang.The developments came after the New York Times reported another alleged relationship between Huang and Nvidia vice president Kimberly Powell, who reports directly to him. The newspaper, citing five people who worked at the company, said the relationship had not been previously reported. The report also raised questions about Nvidia's workplace policies, which ask employees to avoid situations involving potential conflicts of interest, including personal relationships.Read more: Trump administration aware of plans to oust Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang - report Huang, who acknowledged one of the reported relationships in a letter to employees on Sunday, admitted being unfaithful to his wife and apologised for violating their trust. Nvidia's board has reportedly launched an investigation into the matter, led by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz.Huang "was the one who led the marvelous rise of Nvidia," said Bruce Zaro, managing director at Granite Wealth Management in Plymouth, Massachusetts., as quoted by Reuters. "I guess the question would be, can someone step up if Jensen has to resign or is forced out?"Meanwhile, on Wall Street, major US stock indexes ended higher on Wednesday, supported by gains in technology shares after upbeat results from CoreWeave lifted optimism around AI-related investments. The S&P 500 rose 1.31% to 7,619.38, the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.60% to 25,466.19, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 0.49% to 52,486.49. The S&P 500 technology sector climbed 2.7%.
Article Summary: N Nvidia shares fell 8 per cent in after-hours trading on Wednesday. Comes amid reports that the company's board is preparing to discuss the future of CEO Jensen Huang. Reports claim the board is looking for a temporary chief to take over from Huang. Nvidia's stock has come under significant pressure amid the controversy.

Article Title: Rs 3-crore Defender, horse race with SUV prize, 150 dishes: Anant Singh goes all out for daughter's wedding
Article Text:
Mokama MLA Anant Singh is ensuring his daughter’s big day will be difficult to miss.





PATNA: A Rs 3-crore Land Rover Defender for the bridegroom, a BMW worth around Rs 1 crore for the younger son, a wedding venue spread over more than 10 bighas, a horse race with an SUV as the top prize and a menu boasting over 150 dishes.If weddings are about making a statement, Mokama MLA Anant Singh is ensuring his daughter’s big day will be difficult to miss. Add Bollywood and Bhojpuri artists, six models from Dubai and invitations for some of the country’s biggest political names, and the celebrations in Ladma village have become an event with all eyes on it.Known for his flamboyant lifestyle and larger-than-life public persona, Singh is preparing for the Nov 25 wedding of his younger daughter, Shivangi Singh , to Rishikesh Kumar alias Ankit, son of commandant Ranvijay Kumar of Krishnanagar in Bihta, Patna. Rishikesh holds an MBA degree and has lived in the United States for around 11 years.The luxury Defender, estimated to cost between Rs 2.5 crore and Rs 3 crore, has already reached Ladma. The BMW, worth around Rs 1 crore, is for Singh’s youngest son Abhinav, whose ‘janeu’ ceremony will be held alongside the wedding. The vehicles have become a talking point in the village even before the wedding festivities have gathered full pace.The wedding venue is being developed across more than 10 bighas, while a separate ground spread over nearly 12 bighas is being prepared for the horse-racing competition. The scale of the arrangements has prompted Singh to plan for around four lakh visitors, with preparations allowing for the possibility of even more guests.The wedding decorations are being planned on a similarly imposing scale. A nearly 30-foot-high stage, inspired by Jaipur’s Patrakar Chauraha, is being built for the ‘jaimala’ ceremony. Flowers are being sourced from China and Bengaluru, decorative materials from different parts of the country, and tent workers have been brought in from Mau in Uttar Pradesh. A specialised event company has been entrusted with the work.Puneet Kumar, Singh’s eldest son-in-law, said the Defender was chosen by Shivangi and gifted to her on her birthday. She completed her schooling in Delhi and post-graduation from Delhi University.The family has a history of elaborate wedding arrangements. “I was married to Raj Nandini, eldest daughter of Singh, in 2015. In my wedding, only parking was made on around 4 bighas of land,” said the son-in-law.The horse race, scheduled for Nov 25 from 2pm to 4pm, is expected to draw riders from Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana and other states. Manish Kumar, an associate of Singh, said the winner would receive an SUV, the runner-up a motorcycle and the third-place finisher a scooter.Food, too, is being treated as an event in itself. The menu will feature more than 150 varieties, ranging from traditional Bihari preparations to dishes from other states. Sweets will include kaju katli and Silao khaja, the Nalanda speciality known for its distinctive 52-layer structure.Singh has also expressed his wish to invite PM Narendra Modi , former Bihar CM Nitish Kumar, RJD president Lalu Prasad and Tejashwi Prasad Yadav. Assembly Speaker Prem Kumar has already received an invitation.Singh, who has been asked by the Supreme Court to surrender on Dec 4 in Dularchand murder case, has said there will be no political distinction among guests and visitors from anywhere in the world, including India and Pakistan, will be welcome.
Article Summary: Mokama MLA Anant Singh is preparing for the Nov 25 wedding of his younger daughter, Shivangi Singh, to Rishikesh Kumar alias Ankit. The luxury Defender, estimated to cost between Rs 2.5 crore and Rs 3 crore, has already reached Ladma. The BMW, worth around Rs 1 crore, is for Singh’s youngest son Abhinav.

Article Title: Marriage and motherhood should not affect career: Karnataka high court
Article Text:
In an order passed on Oct 29, Justice Lalitha Kanneganti disposed of a petition filed by the woman's husband, who resides in Mumbai (AI Image)

​'Motherhood doesn't confine a woman to single place'​

'

Motherhood doesn

't confine a woman to single place'





BENGALURU: Marriage, motherhood and raising children should not affect a woman's professional career or tie her down to one place, Karnataka high court has observed in a recent judgement, clearing an ophthalmologist's relocation to the United Kingdom.In an order passed on Oct 29, Justice Lalitha Kanneganti disposed of a petition filed by the woman's husband, who resides in Mumbai. He had challenged the order of a Bengaluru family court that directed him to deliver the original passport of their minor child to his wife and provide consent to obtain a visa to travel to the United Kingdom.He had challenged another order rejecting his request for a change in interim custody of the minor child from the wife's family to his family, along with other consequential relief.The wife argued she had been taking care of the child since 2019 when they were thrown out of their residence in Mumbai. According to her, employment in the UK provides a better and more secure financial position, enabling her to provide the child with stable housing, education, healthcare and extracurricular opportunities."Marriage and motherhood do not require her to remain confined to a particular place," the judge said, specifying conditions for mutual visits: The mother shall allow regular audio and video calls between the father and the child at least for 20 minutes a day; the father shall get parenting time with the child during school holidays; twice in a year during the child's holidays, the mother shall send the boy to India to spend 75% of the vacation with the father; the father could go to the United Kingdom to meet the child for 75% of the holidays.
Article Summary: In an order passed on Oct 29, Justice Lalitha Kanneganti disposed of a petition filed by the woman's husband, who resides in Mumbai. He had challenged the order of a Bengaluru family court that directed him to deliver the original passport of their minor child to his wife. The wife argued she had been taking care of the child since 2019.

Article Title: Crackers versus vehicles: What really contributes to Delhi's Diwali pollution?
Article Text:
Vehicles and transport emissions contributed 19% to Delhi’s PM2.5 pollution on the day of the festival, November 8

Diwali fireworks add to existing pollution

Vehicles: An endless source

Diwali fireworks release fine particles that rapidly worsen air quality

Crackers push particulate levels sharply higher

Low wind speeds and temperature inversion make it harder to disperse pollutants

What crackers bring to the table

Delhi's PM2

Weather is the difference

Can't ignore either one





Every year, Delhi’s Diwali pollution debate is between two sources: firecrackers and vehicles. But the latest pollution data suggests the problem is more complex. Pollution can spike sharply in the case of fireworks, but vehicles are one of the biggest contributors to the city’s everyday PM2.5 burden.The real worry is what will happen when these emissions combine with an atmosphere that is already polluted and with bad weather.The Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM) has set up a new Integrated Atmospheric Chemistry and Aerosol Toxicity Analysis Laboratory (AATAL), which gives a useful picture of Delhi’s pollution mix.Vehicles were the single largest contributor to the city’s PM2.5 pollution on Oct. 24, accounting for 25%. Secondary organic aerosols contributed 18.4 %, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols (16.5 %), road dust (10.9 %) and waste burning (5 %).Even around Diwali the transport contribution was still substantial. Vehicles and transport emissions contributed 19% to Delhi’s PM2.5 pollution on the day of the festival, November 8, the largest identified source, estimated the IITM’s Decision Support System (DSS).The figure explains why vehicular pollution cannot be seen as a seasonal problem: unlike fireworks, traffic emissions persist throughout the year.But firecrackers cause pollution of a different kind of episode. They tend to emit their emissions over a relatively short period of time, and they emit fine particles and gasses that can quickly degrade air quality.The effect was visible on the night of Diwali. The Delhi Pollution Control Committee’s data reported on November 9 showed that at Akshardham the PM2.5 concentration was at 760.99 micrograms per cubic meter at 11pm. This was an hourly reading, not a 24 hour average, but gives an idea of how intense the spike of pollution was.Delhi’s AQI had already fallen to 382 on November 6, its worst pre-Diwali reading in eight years, according to CPCB data. It averaged 376 on Diwali November 8, from 369 a day earlier. AQI stood at 368 at 7am on November 9. Of the 54 monitoring stations that reported valid readings, 50 were above 300 and 15 entered the severe category.At the time when fireworks are set off, the Delhi atmosphere is becoming less conducive to dispersing pollutants. The Air Quality Early Warning System said dispersion is difficult when ventilation index is less than 6,000 square meters per second and average wind speeds are below 10kmph. Low temperatures and temperature inversion can also trap pollutants near the ground.That means fireworks smoke doesn’t just disappear when the party’s over. It adds to the existing emissions from vehicles, industry, dust and regional sources, thus adding to the particulate load.The latest figures do not allow for simply blaming either crackers or vehicles. Fireworks are a concentrated blast of pollution to an already stressed atmosphere, but cars carry the burden of emissions daily. Cracker restrictions can curb the festive spike, but sustained improvement will depend on curbing transport emissions, controlling road dust and industrial pollution, and improving regional coordination. One night of action cannot fix a year-long problem of air pollution in Delhi.
Article Summary: Vehicles were the single largest contributor to the city’s PM2.5 pollution on Oct. 24, accounting for 25%. Secondary organic aerosols contributed 18.4 %, followed by secondary inorganic aerosols (16.5%) and road dust (10.9%) Fireworks are a concentrated blast of pollution to an already stressed atmosphere, but cars carry the burden of emissions daily.

Article Title: Samsung set to become South Korea's first company with 200 trillion won in cash
Article Text:
Samsung's cash reserves to cross 200 trillion won as AI chip demand grows

Samsung Electronics is on course to become the first company in South Korea to build cash assets of more than 200 trillion won ($146.6 billion), with the artificial intelligence (AI)-driven semiconductor boom strengthening its financial position.The chipmaker's cash reserves have nearly doubled over the past year, while its overall assets have also grown. The increase comes as Samsung prepares for higher investments in semiconductor manufacturing and research, alongside a sizeable shareholder return programme.Samsung's cash and cash equivalents are estimated to have reached 214.8 trillion won by the end of the third quarter, according to industry data released on Sunday. This marks a rise of 24.8 trillion won from the 190 trillion won recorded at the end of the previous quarter, as reported by Yonhap news agency.The latest estimate is also almost twice the 108.5 trillion won the company held at the end of the third quarter of 2025.Samsung's total assets stood at 791.8 trillion won at the end of September, an increase of 32.4 trillion won over the preceding three months.The company's growing cash position is expected to be enough to cover the highest possible payout under its landmark shareholder return policy announced in August, market watchers estimate.Samsung had indicated that it would make between 90 trillion won and 110 trillion won available for shareholder returns in 2026.The company is also expected to announce its shareholder policy for the coming year at a board meeting scheduled for January.Alongside shareholder payouts, Samsung is preparing for a significant increase in spending on its semiconductor business.Investments in chipmaking infrastructure and research and development are expected to exceed 100 trillion won this year, marking a historic high. Of this amount, 84.4 trillion won is expected to go towards expanding its memory production facilities.Samsung expects the semiconductor supercycle to extend through next year, supported by continued investments in artificial intelligence and a crunch in memory supply.
Article Summary: Samsung's cash and cash equivalents are estimated to have reached 214.8 trillion won by the end of the third quarter, according to industry data released on Sunday. The increase comes as Samsung prepares for higher investments in semiconductor manufacturing and research, alongside a sizeable shareholder return programme.

Article Title: Rupee extends winning streak, breaks below 94 against dollar: What's next
Article Text:
Rupee moves below 94 against US dollar

Crude oil prices cool as hopes of peace grow

Foreign fund inflows add to rupee's support

NEW DELHI: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East.The currency rose 24 paise to 93.74 against the US dollar in early trade. It opened at around 93.85 in the interbank forex market before gaining further. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98 against the greenback.Forex traders said rupee could maintain its positive momentum if diplomatic efforts in the Middle East make progress. Any easing of tensions could reduce the risk premium in crude oil prices, providing further support to the currency.These hopes gained ground over the weekend after US President Donald Trump indicated that further military strikes against Iran were highly unlikely if negotiations progressed and both sides reached a strong agreement.The easing in crude oil prices has been one of the key factors supporting rupee. Brent crude, which had earlier climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. Amit Pabari, managing director of CR Forex Advisors, said improving diplomatic expectations were already having an impact on energy prices."The improvement in diplomatic expectations is already reflecting in energy prices. Brent crude, which had climbed to around $117.64, has now slipped below $100 and is trading near $98. For currency markets, even the possibility of a lasting agreement is important," Pabari said.Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was trading 0.15% lower at $98.17 per barrel in futures trade. The dollar index, which measures the greenback's strength against a basket of six currencies, was also down 0.12% at 102.18.Foreign investment activity provided another source of support for the domestic currency. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) purchased equities worth Rs 13,749.82 crore on Friday, according to exchange data.The combination of lower crude prices and stronger foreign fund inflows has supported the rupee's recent gains against the dollar.With rupee now below the 94-per-dollar level, Pabari sees further room for appreciation. He expects the currency to move towards 93.50 and 93.00, while identifying 94.40–94.50 as the immediate resistance zone."With USD/INR breaking below the 94.00 mark, the probability of further rupee appreciation towards 93.50 and 93.00 has increased. On the upside, 94.40–94.50 is likely to act as the immediate resistance zone," Pabari said.Meanwhile, domestic equity markets opened lower on Monday. BSE Sensex fell 93.95 points to 80,919.19, while NSE Nifty declined 30 points to 24,968.80.Separately, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) reported that India's foreign exchange reserves declined by $2.691 billion to $717.056 billion in the week ended October 30.
Article Summary: Rupee extended its gains for a second straight session on Monday, moving below the 94-per-dollar mark. The rally was supported by softer crude oil prices, stronger foreign fund inflows and hopes of easing tensions in the Middle East. Rupee had already made a strong recovery on Friday, rising 43 paise to close at 93.98.

Article Title: US government is proposing USCIS to bring a new rule that could mean thousands of employees on H-1B visa losing their visa approval
Article Text:
US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)

What is DHS proposing to change

Why DHS wants to end deference policy

H-1B workers could face more requests for evidence

What could the change mean for workers

Thousands of H-1B visa holders and other foreign workers could face closer scrutiny when applying to extend their work status in the US under a new rule proposed by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The proposal would remove a regulation that requires US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to give weight to its own earlier approval when reviewing an extension filed by the same employer for the same worker and job. The proposed change could affect around 208,429 petitions each year, according to DHS estimates cited by immigration law firm Reddy Neuman Brown. H-1B, L-1, O-1, TN and E visa categories would be among those affected. The proposal was published on October 14, 2026, and public comments are due by November 13, 2026.Notably, the rule has not yet been finalized. The existing regulation will remain in effect unless DHS issues a final rule and it takes effect.Under the current regulation, USCIS generally gives deference to a previous approval when an employer files an extension involving the same worker, employer and underlying facts.An officer can move away from the earlier decision if there is a material error, a change in circumstances or new information that affects eligibility.DHS now wants to remove this requirement by deleting Section 8 CFR 214.1(c)(5) and marking the paragraph as “Reserved.” If the proposal becomes final, USCIS officers would be able to review extension applications without being required to rely on the earlier approval. They could reconsider questions that had already been addressed, even if the worker remains in the same role with the same employer.The previous approval could still be considered, but officers would no longer be required to give it deference.DHS says the current policy may shift the burden of proof from employers to USCIS officers. Under immigration law, the petitioner is responsible for proving that a worker qualifies for the requested status. The department also argues that deference could discourage officers from requesting additional evidence when eligibility has not been fully established. It says relying on an earlier approval could allow a questionable decision to influence future petitions.The deference policy was first introduced through a USCIS memo in 2004. USCIS rescinded the memo in 2017, reinstated deference in 2021 and DHS later codified it through the H-1B Modernization Rule in 2024, which took effect in January 2025.H-1B petitions account for more than 75% of all Form I-129 filings, according to DHS. This means H-1B workers could be among the most affected by the proposed change. The removal of deference could lead to more requests for evidence (RFEs) during routine extension applications. USCIS may ask employers to provide additional documents or revisit issues such as whether a job qualifies as a specialty occupation.DHS estimates that the proposal could result in around 6,044 additional RFEs each year. The agency’s analysis also found that denial rates did not statistically differ between periods when deference was in place and periods when it was not. More RFEs could increase the workload for both employers and USCIS, potentially leading to longer processing times.If the proposal is finalized, workers applying for extensions could face more uncertainty, even when their employment details remain unchanged. Additional evidence requests could delay approvals. Longer processing times may also affect workers who plan to travel abroad and need an approved extension before applying for a new visa stamp.Workers whose extensions are filed on time may generally continue working for up to 240 days after their I-94 expires while the application remains pending, subject to applicable rules. Longer processing times could bring more cases closer to this limit.
Article Summary: Proposal would remove regulation that requires USCIS to give weight to its own earlier approval when reviewing an extension filed by the same employer for the same worker and job. The proposed change could affect around 208,429 petitions each year, according to DHS estimates. H-1B, L-1, O-1 and TN and E visa categories would be among those affected.

Article Title: Who is Kimberly Powell, the Nvidia vice president linked to CEO Jensen Huang in second alleged affair
Article Text:
Who is Kimberly Powell? Nvidia vice president named in new report alleging extramarital affair with married CEO Jensen Huang. (NVIDIA Blog)

Kimberly Powell joined Nvidia in 2008

Background in engineering and medical imaging

Key figure in Nvidia's healthcare push

What the report says about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with Kimberly Powell

Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, is now at the centre of a new report about CEO Jensen Huang. According to a recent report by New York Times, Huang also had a relationship with Powell, who reports to him, quoting give people who worked at the company and spoke anonymously. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not yet confirmed the claims. For those unaware, Powell is one of Nvidia’s longest-serving senior executives and have spent more than 18 years at the company and also helped in building its healthcare business into a key growth area for the AI chip giant. Presently, Powell serves as vice president of healthcare at Nvidia where she oversees the company's worldwide healthcare operations. Her responsibilities span hardware and software platforms used for accelerated computing, artificial intelligence, medical imaging, life sciences, drug discovery and healthcare analytics.According to her Nvidia profile, Powell joined the company in 2008 with the goal of establishing Nvidia GPUs as an accelerator platform for medical imaging systems. Over the years, she took on a series of leadership roles as Nvidia expanded beyond graphics processing into AI and high-performance computing applications.Before leading Nvidia's healthcare division, Powell oversaw the company's higher education and research business and was involved with several strategic initiatives, including NVIDIA AI Labs and the NVIDIA Inception startup programme. Her LinkedIn profile identifies her as being based in Santa Clara, California.Powell's career began in engineering and medical imaging technology. In an interview with Healthcare Brew earlier this year, she recalled working with a medical imaging company before joining Nvidia, where she saw first-hand how advances in imaging technology could improve healthcare outcomes. She holds a Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical and Computer Engineering from Northeastern University and has worked across hardware engineering, product management and business development roles focused on medical technology and AIAs Nvidia is working on increasing the role of AI in healthcare, Powell has become company’s most visible executive in this sector. She has also spoken about applications of AI in medical imaging, genomics, drug discovery, clinical research and hospital operations on many occasions. In some of her recent interviews, Powell also stressed on the importance of growing role of generative AI and accelerated computing in helping healthcare organisations to improve clinical workflows, advance research and speed up the development of new treatmentsThe Times said the relationship, which had not been previously reported, was discussed inside Nvidia. Powell is 48 and Huang is 63. When the Times reached Huang by phone and asked about Powell, he said he didn’t think the reporter should be speaking to him directly and hung up. Nvidia did not immediately respond to Reuters’ request for comment.The report came days after Nvidia’s board opened an investigation into Huang over his ties to Alice Huang, a woman US officials believe was recruited by Chinese intelligence. Huang admitted in a message to staff on Sunday that he had been unfaithful to his wife. Shortly after the Times story, the Wall Street Journal reported that the board is preparing to remove him, according to coverage of that report. Nvidia shares fell about 3% in extended trading. President Donald Trump said he had not discussed the allegations with Huang but called him “an honourable guy” who has “done an amazing job for our country.”Nvidia’s code of conduct, which opens with a letter from Huang, lists personal relationships among the situations that can create a conflict of interest. Any relationship between a chief executive and a direct report would raise questions under that policy, as shown in coverage of the code.
Article Summary: Kimberly Powell is one of Nvidia's longest-serving senior executives. She has spent more than 18 years at the company and helped in building its healthcare business into a key growth area for the AI chip giant. According to a recent report by New York Times, Huang also had a relationship with Powell, who reports to him.

Article Title: Why Nvidia stopped telling investors about Singapore sales after cutting off Alice Huang-linked Megaspeed
Article Text:
Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore sales after cutting off Megaspeed

Nvidia switched from billing address to headquarters for country-wise revenue

Megaspeed probe and Alice Huang affair now threaten Jensen Huang’s job

Nvidia quietly stopped reporting its Singapore revenue in late 2025, months after it cut off Megaspeed International, the Singapore-based cloud company now at the heart of the espionage scandal around CEO Jensen Huang. The timing, flagged by The Wall Street Journal, raises fresh questions about how much investors could see of Nvidia’s sales tied to a market that was briefly one of its biggest.In the quarter ending July 2025, Singapore brought in $10.2 billion, or 22% of Nvidia’s total revenue, up 81% from a year earlier. Two years before that, its share was just 8%. A quarter later, the line had vanished from Nvidia’s filings. An Nvidia spokesperson told the WSJ that Megaspeed was put on an internal block list in June 2025, barring further sales and shipments. The company has not said whether the two moves are connected.From the quarter ending October 2025, Nvidia began assigning revenue by where a customer is headquartered rather than where it is billed. It said the change “provides a better representation of the geographic profile of our revenue.”The old breakdown listed the US, Singapore, Taiwan, China (including Hong Kong) and “other”. The new one kept every line except Singapore.Recast figures suggest most Singapore-billed revenue moved into the US column, while China and Taiwan were revised higher.The WSJ points to a hole in that logic. Nvidia had earlier said Singapore was used mainly for centralised invoicing, with products “almost always shipped elsewhere.” A headquarters address says no more about where chips land. Nvidia spokesperson Patrick Rutherford declined to say where Megaspeed’s sales were booked under either method, or whether dropping Singapore was linked to the block.Servers from US firms like Dell and Super Micro add another layer. Many buyers get Nvidia chips inside these systems, and it is unclear whether those deals count as US revenue wherever the machines end up.In August 2025, between the block and the reporting change, Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter emailed Commerce Department agents investigating Megaspeed, saying a senior department official had cleared him to reach out, according to The New York Times. The case was soon handed to the Justice Department, which is running a criminal inquiry. In October 2025, President Trump was briefed that Megaspeed executive Alice Huang was presumed to be a Chinese intelligence asset close to Jensen Huang, the NYT reported.Trade records cited by the NYT show Megaspeed’s Malaysian sister firm Speedmatrix bought at least $4.8 billion of AI equipment containing Nvidia chips between June 2024 and February 2026, well past the June 2025 cutoff and often through intermediaries. Megaspeed denies illegally moving chips to China.Huang has since admitted the affair and apologised to employees. Nvidia’s board is investigating whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, and the WSJ has reported that the board is preparing to oust him.Without a Singapore line, Nvidia’s filings cannot show whether cutting off Megaspeed dented sales or barely registered. Either answer would have invited the questions the company is now facing anyway.
Article Summary: N Nvidia stopped reporting Singapore sales after cutting off Megaspeed. Company switched from billing address to headquarters for country-wise revenue.Megaspeed is now at the heart of the espionage scandal around CEO Jensen Huang. Nvidia has not said whether the two moves are connected.

Article Title: ‘LinkedIn Premium subscriptions, MacBooks and more’: Canva CEO offers ‘different’ support package after announcing major job cuts
Article Text:
Canva layoffs and restructuring will affect 1,271 people which is about 22% of its global workforce.

What’s in Canva’s support package

Read the message by Canva CEO:

Supporting those who are leaving

We know everyone's circumstances are different, and while nothing can make today’s news easy, we've tried to reflect those different needs in the financial, career and wellbeing support we're providing to everyone affected:

Everyone will receive at least six months of salary, inclusive of statutory entitlements, regardless of location.

Removing the one-year vesting cliff for those who joined in the past year.

Twelve months of continued healthcare coverage in countries where we currently provide this.

Twelve months of Canva Care (our EAP), with this coverage also extending to family members.

Dedicated career support, including one-on-one coaching, interview preparation, and one year of LinkedIn Premium. We're also dedicating a significant portion of our Talent Acquisition team to helping people review their resumes and practice for interviews to find their next opportunity.

An opt-in alumni talent directory that we'll proactively share with our investors, partners, and wider industry network to help connect departing Canvanauts with new roles.

Everyone leaving will be able to keep their Canva MacBook as we know not everyone has a personal laptop.

We’re also launching the Canva Collective Fund, providing US$10,000 grants to departing Canvanauts who want to start something of their own. Whether it’s starting a business or doing something meaningful for their local community, the fund is designed to help get those ideas off the ground. Everyone leaving as part of these changes will have until the 14 of December to register their interest, and we won’t take any ownership or equity in what they create.

Australian design software company Canva recently announced that it is cutting 1,271 jobs, roughly 22% of its global workforce, as it grapples with slowing growth and prepares for a major internal overhaul. Co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins broke the news in a lengthy message to staff, which was later published on the company’s newsroom website. Perkins apologised to affected employees for the pain and disruption caused by the restructuring. The cuts will touch teams across all 37 countries where Canva operates. While many employees will be asked to move into new roles or relocate to centralised office hubs, others will be leaving the company. To those leaving, the company has offered a support package that may be different from others.To soften the blow for departing staff, Canva outlined an extensive severance and support package. Regardless of where they live, employees leaving the company will receive at least six months of salary (including statutory entitlements) and up to 12 months of healthcare coverage, where applicable.Along with this, the company is offering departing workers to keep their Canva-issued MacBooks.Moreover, they will receive LinkedIn Premium subscriptions, alongside access to an alumni talent network, and access to career coaching and interview preparation for career help. Canva is also launching the “Canva Collective Fund,” which will offer$10,000 grants to eligible departing employees who want to start their own businesses or community projects.
Article Summary: Australian design software company Canva announced that it is cutting 1,271 jobs, roughly 22% of its global workforce. Co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins broke the news in a lengthy message to staff, which was later published on the company’s newsroom website. To soften the blow, Canva outlined an extensive severance and support package.

Article Title: Jeff Bezos' father fled Cuba with 3 shirts at 16; 33 years later, he and his wife invested $250,000 of their savings in Amazon, a bet that could now be worth more than the GDP of 100 countries
Article Text:
Image: Getty Images

Jeff Bezos’ father fled Cuba as a teenager under Operation Pedro Pan

From a refugee camp to a career at Exxon

How Jeff Bezos' parents invested nearly $250,000 in Amazon

Amazon's growth transformed the value of its early shares

The value of the Bezos family's Amazon investment

Miguel and Jackie Bezos' philanthropic work

At 16, Miguel Bezos left Cuba for the United States with just three shirts, three pairs of trousers, a pair of shoes and a handmade jacket. Arriving as an unaccompanied teenager during a period of political upheaval in Cuba, he had to rebuild his life in a country where he did not even speak the language. Over the next three decades, he completed his education, established a career in engineering and management, and started a family. In 1995, 33 years after leaving Cuba, he and his wife, Jackie Bezos, invested nearly $250,000 of their hard-earned savings in their son Jeff Bezos ' fledgling online bookstore, Amazon, despite being warned that they could lose the entire amount. That early investment, based on subsequent stock splits and assuming the original shares were retained, could be worth more than $90 billion today, exceeding the annual GDP of more than 100 countries.Born in Santiago de Cuba, Miguel Bezos left his home country in 1962 as part of Operation Pedro Pan, a programme that enabled thousands of Cuban children to travel to the United States without their parents. The migration took place amid concerns among Cuban families about the political changes following Fidel Castro's rise to power. Many parents believed sending their children to America would give them access to better opportunities and a safer future.Miguel arrived in Miami on July 21, 1962, at the age of 16. According to an account published by Amazon, he carried three shirts, three pairs of trousers, a pair of shoes and a handmade jacket. His mother had made the jacket using cleaning cloths because the family had limited resources.He initially stayed at Camp Matecumbe, a refugee centre in Florida, before being transferred to a Catholic institution in Wilmington, Delaware. His parents expected their separation to be temporary, but Miguel had to begin adapting to an unfamiliar country, a different culture and a language he did not know.Miguel continued his education in the United States, attending Salesianum School in Wilmington, Delaware. He later received a scholarship to the University of Albuquerque in New Mexico, where he studied mathematics and graduated in 1968.During his university years, he met Jacklyn Gise, known as Jackie. The couple married in 1968. Jackie already had a son, Jeff Bezos, from her previous marriage. Miguel adopted Jeff when he was four years old, becoming his father and helping raise him.After graduating, Miguel built a professional career in engineering and management at Exxon. He worked for the energy company for more than three decades, taking up positions that provided financial stability for his family. His experience as an immigrant who had rebuilt his life through education and professional work would later form an important part of the Bezos family's story.In 1994, Jeff Bezos decided to leave his job at investment firm D E Shaw and pursue an opportunity he saw in the rapidly expanding internet. He moved to establish an online bookstore, which would eventually become Amazon.His parents became among his earliest financial backers. In February 1995, Miguel personally invested $100,000 in the company. A separate investment of $145,500 followed in July 1995 through Jackie's family trust. Together, their contributions amounted to approximately $245,500, commonly rounded to $250,000.The decision involved a considerable financial risk. Jeff later recalled warning his parents that there was a 70% chance they could lose their entire investment. He also remembered that his father initially asked him what the internet was, as the technology was still unfamiliar to many people at the time.Despite the uncertainty, Miguel and Jackie decided to support their son. Jeff later explained that his parents were investing in him rather than simply betting on the idea of an online bookstore. Their decision came at a time when Amazon was still a small start-up with no guarantee of becoming a successful business.Amazon launched its online bookstore in July 1995, initially selling books to customers through its website. The business expanded rapidly, receiving orders from all 50 US states and 45 countries within its first 30 days.The company went public in May 1997 at $18 per share, raising approximately $54 million. Over the following years, Amazon expanded beyond books into electronics, clothing, cloud computing, entertainment and other services, becoming one of the world's largest technology companies.Its growth also increased the potential value of shares acquired by its earliest investors. Amazon carried out four stock splits: a 2-for-1 split in 1998, two additional splits in 1999, and a 20-for-1 split in 2022. Together, these increased the original share count 240 times.The stock splits meant that early shareholders who retained their holdings would own substantially more shares than they originally purchased, although the value of each individual share adjusted accordingly.Based on the original share purchases and the cumulative effect of Amazon's stock splits, the combined parental investment of approximately $245,500 could theoretically represent around 343.3 million shares.Using an illustrative Amazon closing price of $266.93 on November 9, 2026, the original combined shareholding would have a hypothetical value of approximately $91.63 billion, assuming all the original shares had been retained.The figure offers a striking comparison with the annual economic output of entire countries. According to World Bank data, Panama's nominal gross domestic product was approximately $90.46 billion in 2025. The hypothetical value of the original investment would therefore be slightly higher than Panama's annual GDP.At that valuation, the investment would also exceed the annual GDP of more than 100 countries and economies, depending on the GDP dataset and year used. The comparison illustrates the scale of Amazon's growth from a small online bookstore into a global technology business.Beyond their involvement in Amazon's early years, Miguel and Jackie Bezos also established a philanthropic presence through the Bezos Family Foundation, which they co-founded in 2000. The foundation supports initiatives focused on education, child development and opportunities for young people.The family has also donated substantial Amazon holdings over the years. Reports have documented transfers of Amazon shares to the foundation between 2001 and 2016, reflecting the couple's involvement in philanthropic activities as the company grew.Miguel's journey from an unaccompanied Cuban teenager arriving in America with a few belongings to an engineer, father and early Amazon investor has remained an important part of the history behind the company.
Article Summary: Miguel Bezos fled Cuba as a teenager under Operation Pedro Pan. He arrived in Miami in 1962 with just three shirts, three pairs of trousers, a pair of shoes and a handmade jacket. Over the next three decades, he completed his education, established a career in engineering and management, and started a family. In 1995, 33 years after leaving Cuba, he and his wife, Jackie Bezos, invested nearly $250,000 of their hard-earned savings in their son Jeff Bezos'fledgling online bookstore, Amazon.

Article Title: Meta’s head of Infrastructure, Engineering Santosh Janardhan is leaving the company after 15 years; says in an internal memo: Time to pass ...
Article Text:
A long-time Amazon's cloud unit executive, Dave Brown joined Meta in July 2026

Meta Platforms' longtime infrastructure head will leave the company in early 2027. Santosh Janardhan, Meta’s head of infrastructure and co-head of engineering, told the company's employees that he would step down from leading the infrastructure organization, according to a memo obtained by Bloomberg News. He did not detail the reasons for his departure in the message.Janardhan, who has worked at Meta since 2009, said “it’s time to pass the baton” to former AWS senior vice president David Brown , who joined Meta in July from AWS. Janardhan said in the memo that he will help support Brown through the first quarter of 2027 as part of “the transition.” He wrote, “As we make the next set of choices about our priorities, this is the right time for Dave to take the lead in shaping that work." Janardhan added in the memo, “Dave has spent his career building and operating dependable infrastructure for a wide range of demanding workloads. He has the instincts, depth and judgment this moment requires.”The announcement means that Brown will now formally lead Meta’s infrastructure efforts and serve as chief technical officer of the Meta Compute initiative, which is spearheaded by the company’s president and vice chairman Dina Powell McCormick and technical leader Daniel Gross.Dave Brown joined Meta in July 2026. Previously, he was senior vice president in Amazon Web Services. Brown joined AWS in its initial days and was a member of the early team that assembled its core EC2 service in South Africa in the 2000s. EC2, one of AWS’ oldest services, provides virtual slices of physical servers for rent, billed by the second, that companies use to run applications and websites. He was also part of Amazon CEO Andy Jassy’s S-team. Jassy's S-team is reported to be a highly influential group of 28 executives with whom CEO Jassy meets regularly to make key business decisions.According to analysts, the change of guard underscores Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s efforts to expand the company’s data center operations under newer leaders at a time of increasing investor scrutiny on capital expenditure spending by the social media giant and its hyperscaler rivals.This major leadership change comes as Meta continues to invest hundreds of billions of dollars in artificial intelligence and the data centers needed to support it.During its third quarter earnings report, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, said, "We hit major milestones this quarter toward delivering personal superintelligence for everyone - including launching Muse and Muse Wonder, our first frontier model.” It added that it expects full-year capex to fall in the range of $135 billion to $145 billion. Meta also logged negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion, which S&P Global Ratings noted as part of its decision in late October to revise Meta’s credit rating from AA- stable to AA- negative.
Article Summary: Santosh Janardhan, Meta’s head of infrastructure and co-head of engineering, told the company's employees that he would step down from leading the infrastructure organization. He did not detail the reasons for his departure in the message. Dave Brown joined Meta in July from Amazon Web Services.

Article Title: Colette Kress, Ian Buck and five others who could be Nvidia’s next CEO as the company prepares to fire Jensen Huang
Article Text:
Who replaces Jensen Huang?

Nvidia’s flat structure left no obvious successor to Jensen Huang

Colette Kress is the safest pair of hands for the interim job

Ian Buck has the strongest claim among the engineers

Rene Haas is the outsider who already knows the culture

Johny Srouji would bring Apple's chip discipline

Eric Schmidt is the caretaker some would reach for

Madison Huang is the family name with the most visible rise

Nico Caprez, Huang’s son-in-law, has become the family's power broker
